0) Update release notes (using AI)

Prompt: 

Copilot, please generate an entry for the file #file:'C:\Dev\fpl.net\Fpl\RELEASE_NOTES.md'  that summarizes the changes from the file #file:'C:\Dev\fpl.net\Fpl\CHANGELOG.md'.
between the versions [provide new version number] (next to-be-released version) 
and the version [provide the last published version number] (last publicly released version). 

Please group the release notes for this release by the tags following the convention you can already find in 
RELEASE_NOTES.md: While the CHANGELOG.md is outlined using the hierarchy 
version number -> change type -> tag, 
the release notes should be outlined using the hierarchy 
release number -> tag.

The preferred order the tags is (if applicable): [parser], [interpreter], [language-server], [vscode], [other]

It suffices to output only the single release note with this version number (no re-printing the existing release notes for other versions is needed).

1) 
Before testing the extension with VS Code (F5): run this command to ensure you have the latest release of the language server:
npm run vscode:prepublish

2) 
If you only want to test the DLL refresh step in isolation (without recompiling TypeScript), just run:
npm run copy-ls-dlls

(both steps will recreate the folder ./out/FplLsDll with its contents copied from the .net Release)
This is a good way to sanity-check that dotnet publish succeeds and that out/FplLsDll gets populated correctly before you commit to running the full vsce package/vsce publish flow, which also does packaging/upload work you may not want to repeat unnecessarily.

3)
When checking the list files to be packed with vsce, run 
npx vsce ls

4)
When finally publishing the extension, run
vsce package
vsce publish
